subclassFeature.name: Path of Precognition
entries: {@i "… I've already waited way past with what anyone oughta put up with. And right when I thought I was finally getting my ass outta this goddamn cold, what happens? My Ticket turns into blank scrap paper, all because of that mongrel brat! Ha… Haha… Gimme a fucking break."}

You have found a powerful relic capable of seeing a few seconds into the future, and you have repurposed it into one of your eyes so that your enemies never reach you again. When it overheats, so does your rage, allowing you to hit your enemies with incredible might as a practicioner of La Spada di Palermo, a powerful and fast sword style that confuses most opponents.

You are a washed-up member of the Thumb, a powerful criminal syndicate that values hierarchy above all else. Maybe you were a powerful leader that fell from grace, or you never amounted to much to begin with, but the Thumb has assigned you to be one of the lowest of the low.

Barbarians from the Path of Precognition tend to believe they know everything, and all outcomes were obvious for them. At their best, they are wise leaders that guide their underlings to be their best. At their worst, they're manipulative and vindictive, trying

subclassFeature.name: The Eye of Precognition
entries: {@i "What, having a hard time landing a hit?"}
You have 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. While you have counts of this, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet
Your Armor Class increases by 3

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature misses an attack against you due to your AC bonus, and 5 counts whenever you take no damage after succeeding on a Dexterity saving throw.

Once you lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. While you have counts of this, you gain the following characteristics:

items: You always roll an additional damage die of the weapon you are attacking with
Your Armor Class decreases by 3
Whenever taking Fire damage, take an additional damage die of the same value as your eye socket burns.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature hits an attack against you due to your AC decrease, and 3 counts whenever you take additional Fire damage from a hostile source. Once you lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and gain up to 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

subclassFeature.name: Colpi di Taglio
entries: {@i "… I've already waited way past what anyone oughta put up with. And right when I thought I was finally getting my ass outta this goddamn cold, what happens? My Ticket turns into blank scrap paper, all because of that mongrel brat! Ha… Haha… Gimme a fucking break."}
This is done through dual weapons, allowing you to make perfected use of Two-Weapon Fighting:

items: You may wield two weapons without the prerequisite of one of them being Light, instead only requiring that neither weapon is Heavy.

Whenever you make an {@action Attack} as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules you still add half your ability modifier to the damage dealt. Whenever you do so, you choose whether you inflict 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on your target, or triggering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Upon reaching level 10, this count increases to 4.
When you Attune to a pair of magical weapons, they both count as a singular Attunement, taking only one slot and becoming Unattuned if either Attunement is broken.

entries: Additionally, whenever a creature misses you with an attack you may spend your Reaction to use {@i Sezionatura di Coniglio} as an attack against that creature. You may do so an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.
When entering your Rage, you may use {@i Sezionatura di Coniglio} as an attack against a creature within range without expending a use of the feature.

entries.name: Sezionatura di Coniglio
entries: On a hit, you deal damage as usual and the creature suffers 1 count of both {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you are raging, you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Creatures that are Small or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: The Shame of My Famiglia
entries: {@i "… Tsk. Great. Not a single damn idiot left to call over for a drink… Bunch of weak-ass pushovers. Got chewed up by those disgusting bugs and died like trash."}

You have lost a position of power important to you, or perhaps something similar, and it has been difficult for you to recover ever since. You have advantage on saving throws against becoming drunk. You refuse to drink {@item ale (gallon)|PHB|Ale}, but after consuming an entire {@item Fine Wine (bottle)|PHB|bottle of Fine Wine}, you may choose to immediately become affected by the {@condition Drunk|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition for 1 minute. You gain the following characteristics when affected by the {@condition Drunk|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition:

items: You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks, Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws and ranged attacks.
As a bonus action, you can yell at one of your allies to do better, granting them advantage on their next ability check, saving throw or attack roll, your choice

When you hit a creature that is {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremoring}, or Both, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} die of damage of equal damage to your weapon's damage type
You can substitute one of your attacks for a {@i Sezionatura di Cervo}.

entries.name: Sezionatura di Cervo
entries: On a hit, you deal damage as usual and the creature suffers 1 count of both {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you are raging, you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Creatures that are Medium or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Accelerating Future
entries: {@i "Feelin' confident? Then parry this, asshole."}

As a battle drives on, you have learned how to mark your favored enemies, focusing all of your wrath on a specific being instead of lashing out wildly like a volcano. You may choose to make the last creature you attacked on your turn become your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. When you hit your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with an attack roll, once per turn, you may choose to convert all of their counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremor Scorch}. Furthermore, whenever you apply counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they suffer 1 additional count of each applied.

Additionally, you have learned how to devote extra energy to your {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to calculate the most likely outcome of the near future. As an action, you can expend 5 counts of your {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to see 1 minute into the future and discover what the most possible outcomes are. Alternatively, by suffering 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion}, you can see 10 minutes into the future instead.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This ability is left more vague on purpose for DMs and players to have more fun with it, however, I think it's important to give an example of how it can and can't be used to make it clearer.

Let's say you're trying to find out what to bet on in a cassino, or what an NPC will say before they say it - those things are fully under the DM's control and he should be able to disclose the most likely future according to the perception of your eye.

However, things outside of the DM's control, such as what a player character would do/say or the outcome of a combat decided by the dice, are much less likely to be predicted, so your eyes can provide an incorrect assessment of the furure, or no assessment at all.

subclassFeature.name: Sezionatura di Elefante
entries: {@i "… Tsk. Great. Not a single damn idiot left to call over for a drink… Bunch of weak-ass pushovers. Got chewed up by those disgusting bugs and died like trash."}

You swing your blade with enough strength and speed to leave even the wisest of men unable to comprehend your movements without slowing them down. While raging, you may perform an additional bonus action attack as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules, however, this attack only inflicts 1 count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Furthermore, you gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and creatures that are Large or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll. If you managed to hit the same creature with all four of your attacks, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or suffer the effects of the {@spell Confusion} spell until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Disposal
entries: If you managed to hit the same creature with all four of your attacks and that creature is your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on that creature twice, only expending all counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after the second burst. If that kills it, you may perform this ability one more time. Otherwise, you may only perform this ability once per Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Fluttering Life Domain
entries: {@i "Where do humans go upon the final egress from life? You ask a rather stimulating question. I have once written my reflections on the end of life; perhaps we may have a chance to discuss it later."}

A buttefly soars freely through the world, needing not the wind to propel its sails nor a great will to guide its whims. Those who have chosen to dutifully follow the domain of a Fluttering Life srive to be much like that, to find, enact and nurture this freedom to live life through all the sorrows that death brings, acting often not as evangelists but instead as travelling undertakers and funeral orators.

They, at their worst, may come off as stark or even have a downlifting aura about their dour workings, yet when allowed to practice freely they usually become stalwart pillars of comfort and calm enforcers of welcoming acceptance of passing on.

In worlds such as Eberron, these first rose from the cracked ground as manifestation of the battlefields - Undead beings of solidified sorrows that roamed the earth and passed down their teachings not to end undeath of itself, but to finally allow those that couldn't to finally find peace. In others, such as that of the grim lands of Balefire beat their boots through the entire world as a rare, unseen sight - Preventing the malaise of souls from spreading by exhuming the bodies of the fallen and being one of the few, few people who fight back flame not with more flame, but instead with extinguishing the pain that yet assails the world.

subclassFeature.name: Blink, Gone
entries: {@i "It would have been nice to have those who would lament my passing, yet the remembrance of the dead has no place in the hearts of those who live here."}

The butterflies of the afterlife have come to rest their weary wings upon your shoulders, much as you have been trained and ordained as a grave keeper of sorts - caring and nurturing for the dead and passing on of the world. These butterflies, spirits of transience, have chosen to aid you in your goals just as you aid them - Whenever you make a hit a creature you inflict {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. Whenever you hit multiple hostile creatures with a spell or they fail a saving throw from your spells you instead cause each creature to suffer an amount of {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} equal to half your proficiency bonus plus the spell slot level consumed, split equally amongst every target of the spell. ( To a minimum of one. )

Additionally, these butterflies that surround you have a tendency to perch upon the bodies of those that linger to pass on, giving you Advantage on {@skill Insight} and {@skill Perception} checks to perceive a creature as being of the Undead type. Furthermore, if you cast the {@spell Find Familiar} spell you may choose to summon your familiar as a kaleidoscope of these butterflies, a group that remains with you for prolonged periods of time. These use the {@creature Owl} stat sheet except they are a Medium swarm of Tiny Undead and have the {@i Tranquillity} trait appended to their sheet, as per what is presented below.

entries.name: Tranquillity
entries: The Kaleidoscope of Dead Butterflies uses your Spellcasting modifier, including any bonuses from magical divine foci, to their {@skill Insight} checks to detect the presence of Undead creatures within 15-ft. of themselves and to discern another creatures Alignment. They may report back to you any information gleamed this way through ethereal whispers of a gentle nature.

subclassFeature.name: Celebration for the Departed
entries: {@i "The barrel of the gun does not fire bullets of butterflies; it is merely that butterflies, both living and dead, bloom from where the gun points."}

The memory of fireworks is one that warms the hearts of many people, calling to attention a blast of heat that warms the heart as much as it does the body. You might have come to harbour something near such memories, yet the principle of a spectacle to remark on the importance of life isn't ever lost on you, and that manifests in your weapons of choice. You gain proficiency in Firearms and due to a gathering of knowledge pertaining to celebrations and ceremonies, you are uniquely qualified to preside over funerals and to safely guide souls to a peaceful afterlife.

You may perform funeral rites over a period of at least an hour, granting a lifted weight for the living, yet guaranteeing the restfulness of the dead. The dead subject of this ceremony cannot be revived through any means other than {@spell True Resurrection} under the condition of the spirit being willing as well and may not be contacted through means such as the {@spell Speak with Dead} spell.

To properly complete this ritual you need at least the body of a deceased creature or an item of great importance of the dead. They may be of undead type, but must be Unconscious and willing for the whole duration to become departed.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Extended Spells
entries: {@i "I fear letting even the lightest wisp of frivolity upon this lament... Thus, it's only right that I wreath solemnness upon my heart as I pull their triggers."}

The domain which presides upon the transient state of life unto death concerns itself on the matters regarding both the living and the departed equally, seeing to guide any lingering spirits to the great beyond and make sure any funeral procession goes accomplished without issue.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Solemn Lament for the Living
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to summon and unseal a great coffin that leads into where the dead go to rest, then retrieving the tools for your grave keeping amongst the living.
As an action, you raise your holy symbol and cause a coffin to raise from ethereal mists, then grab one of the following weapons of your choice:

entries.name: Condolences and Eternal Rest
entries: You retrieve a pair of twin revolvers that remain in inverse colours to one another, a set of tools to reap life from those that should remain dead. These have the {@itemProperty Light}, Range (30/60-ft.) and {@itemProperty Reload|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} (6) weapon properties and deal {@damage 1d8} of your choice of radiant or necrotic damage.

entries.name: Quiet Coffin. ( Requires at least 8th Level. )
entries: You forgo simply retrieving a weapon from the inside of the coffin, instead grabbing the coffin itself and shifting its material form to be that of a heavy machine gun. It has the {@itemProperty Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burst Fire} (PB), {@itemProperty Heavy}, {@itemProperty Reload|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} (PB) and {@itemProperty Two-Handed|PHB|Two-handed} weapon properties, yet whenever you take the {@action Attack} Action using this weapon you have a reach of a 45-ft. cone starting from you instead of having to select a single target. You roll a single attack roll whose result is considered against the AC of all hostile creatures within that reach, dealing your choice of {@damage 1d4} radiant or necrotic damage. If you make use of this weapon's {@itemProperty Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burst Fire} feature you may only select one target for all your attacks.

All these weapons count as divine foci for you, Whenever the {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Condition would be inflicted through your spells and you are using weapons from this Channel Divinity as your divine focus, you use your full proficiency bonus instead of half that value. ( Whenever aiming at a single or multiple targets. ) And provided you are wielding these weapons only, you inflict an additional {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count whenever you deal damage to a target
To reload these weapons you use no form of bullet, instead relying on the dead butterflies that kindly offer themselves as a source of ammunition.
These weapons also grow in power in tandem with you, becoming +1 magic weapons when you reach 5th level, +2 at 10th level and a +3 at 17th level.

Lastly, these weapons remain corporeal for one minute until they dissipate in thin air. For the duration you may summon a kaleidoscope of butterflies to aid you in locating the dead and undead within a range of 300-ft times the magic weapon bonus you gain from this feature, instantly allowing you to find the general direction of the aforementioned beings provided they are not actively entombed through walls of stone or metal that are at least 5-ft.
{@i He's carrying a coffin. A large coffin to pay tribute to the employees who have nowhere else to go. It is still too small to comfort those innocent sacrifices.}

subclassFeature.name: To Embrace a Fleeting Moment in Life Toward Stillness of Death
entries: {@i "Well do I understand your sentiment on death. Why not lay rest to the impulses in your heart for a moment and converse with me more?"}

Even in a fight you've trained your thoughts to remain calm, to be a guiding light to all those around you. This training has also resulted in a demeanour that pacifies the pain in one's ailing mind to provide at least a moment's clarity. You gain a +2 bonus modifier on {@skill Insight} and Charisma skill checks regarding conversing with the Undead and while within 10-ft. of you, they regain at least the faintest hint of their memories and personality. - enough to enable conversation in the first place. Additionally you may use your Bonus Action to calm Undead creatures and similarly unliving beings. All Undead creatures within 60-ft. that can hear you must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC or become {@condition Charmed} by you and non-hostile toward creatures that haven't attacked them for the next minute, awakening some spark of sentience in them.

You do not gain this feature's skill check bonus modifier if the Undead are actively hostile to you or if you have dealt damage to them within the past hour. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

Whenever you calm Undead in this way, a butterfly perches upon the shoulder of the yet-to-be-departed, granting them a +1 bonus to Wisdom saving throws and they may choose to spend their Action to instantly die in peace. Upon reaching 20th level in this subclass, whenever a creature dies this way any curse or negative effect of your choice that would be caused, activated or maintained is instantly negated and lifted.

You may give these butterflies to friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you as a Bonus Action, spending an use of the feature. An ally remains with a butterfly for a minute before it flutters off, gaining the same Wisdom saving throw bonus and reducing any {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count they suffer by one. ( To a minimum of one. )
These bonus modifiers to your skill checks and Wisdom saving throws is increased by 1 upon you reaching 12th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: Hallowed Strikes
entries: {@i "It is a heavy gift that I shoulder a twain of wayward souls in each of my palms, fingers held ever-closer."}

At 8th level, the cleric gains the ability to infuse their weapon strikes with a mixture of balancing energy. Once on each of the cleric's turns when they hit a creature with a weapon attack, the cleric can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage to the target whenever they deal radiant damage, and the inverse when dealing necrotic damage. When the cleric reaches 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d4}.

subclassFeature.name: Goodbye Now, A Sorrow in You
entries: {@i "At the heart of a broken mirror, I see the fading butterfly. A wandering butterfly I cannot bloom, yet the duty of lamentation is mine, thus, it is also mine, this melancholy."}

You come to reach a point where you lead a calm life despite all that assails your life, embracing the transience of life as a simple fact, much like day slips into night and night to day. To that end, your lectures toward the dead have come to be an aura that follows you to the ends of the earth. You gain the following:

items: Whenever a creature that you can see dies within 60-ft. of you a small collection of butterflies crowd toward you, granting you two {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. This Condition has no effect on you and does not change or diminish at the end of your turns, instead you gain a +1 bonus modifier to Wisdom saving throws for each 4 count you currently have, to a maximum of +3. Whenever you would inflict {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} on a creature, you may choose to spend from your count to add the same amount to theirs.
You always have the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell prepared and may cast it at will without spending a spell slot.

Creatures that you lay to rest ( through killing or through use of any of your features ) may choose to linger on as a butterfly, using the {@creature Owl} stat sheet except they may speak telepathically through any language they knew in life and they instantly die when wandering further than 360-ft. of you. They become neutral toward you if they were hostile but are otherwise friendly and calm toward you. You may use their butterfly body to revive them through a {@spell Resurrection} or greater spell without requiring their original body.

subclassFeature.name: Way of Crumbling Enlightenment
entries: {@i "Remember not only to refill what you have burned out but also to add new knowledge into your repositories.”"}

Knowledge and the body are an organism when in combination, the brain's synapses leading to the fists clenching and bursting forward in a coordinated transfer of energy for devastating power. Monks who dwell in the sects of Enlightenment know this well, and cultivate their minds to accumulate as much intelligence as possible, then taking it apart crumb by crumb to fuel their arts.

Often cloistered with their fellows, these are also the keepers of vast reliquaries that do well in archival and retrieval of all manner of great item that was misplaced or forlorn to time, also holding out special holdings in the nourishing of young minds within their ranks, often acting as orphanages just as well.

entries.subclassFeature: Gathering of Knowledge as Kindling|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: Gathering of Knowledge as Kindling
entries: {@i "Remember not only to refill what you have burned but also to add new knowledge into your repositories."}

Your free time is often spent in the dwellings of books, absorbing knowledge as if it were oxygen. Whenever you take a long rest you may choose to become Proficient in two skills you weren't Proficient with, then having these Proficiencies lost at the next long rest as the knowledge fades from your mind as you make space for more.

Yet the wisdom imparted to you is left not only in theory, but also used to glimpse {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}s of the world and its ways in a practical manner. You may do the following to gain counts of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, which is used to fuel certain abilities or to passively bolden yourself:

items: You may spend a Bonus Action to instantly forget one of your skill Proficiencies, gaining 2 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count.
You may spend a Bonus Action to instantly forget one of your Artisan's Tools, Instrument or Gaming Kit Proficiencies, gaining 1 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count.

entries: Whenever you forget a proficiency you effectively juxtapose that piece of knowledge to re-frame the world in front of you, aiding in the connection and conceptualization of ideas you may not have seen before, yet you also forget the original purpose of this piece of intelligence, having its base set to crumble within the annals of your mind. You lose the ability to use your proficiency bonus in rolls regarding the lost proficiency until the end of your next long rest.

While you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you gain a bonus modifier to unarmed attacks and Intelligence skill checks equal to half of your current count of the Condition. Additionally, you gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence saving throws and skill checks equal to your current count. You may have a maximum count of the Condition equal to your proficiency bonus.

If you spend Ki to perform an ability that requires you to have a minimum amount of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you lose one count at the end of your turns. Otherwise, your count is reduced by one per minute spent outside of combat.

subclassFeature.name: Means of Cultivation
entries: {@i "Grow your knowledge. Use exams to motivate and push yourselves further. Only then shall you one day be permitted an audience with the Saints."}

Upon reaching 3rd level in Monk, choose which way you will proceed to acquire your knowledge with - a perception-bending key to your knowledge or to hold and tear it off with your bare hands. You gain the chosen 3rd level feat and a corresponding one upon reaching 11th level.

entries.subclassFeature: To Grasp Erudition With One's Own Hands (Fist)|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3
To Behold Light Through a Gilded Keyhole (Key)|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: To Behold Light Through a Gilded Keyhole (Key)
entries: {@i "I'm sure you would like to know more about this… key. Hmm~ How do I put this? It's a medium…? A vessel for knowledge…? Kinda hard to explain to someone who hasn't used it before."}

You are of a sect which makes use of special relics to glimpse newfound expertise directly, being one of the select number who learnt how to maximize learning in this way. You carry a gigantic Key of Knowledge, a magic item you are permanently attuned to that doesn't count toward your attunement limit. You gain the following benefits when you choose this feature:

items: Your Key of Knowledge counts as a monk weapon for you and you deal an additional 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on weapon attacks while wielding it. This increases by one upon reaching 8th level in this class.

Like the library of your mind, your Key may expand as needed to destroy things in your path. You may consume one {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count at the end of your turn to expand the Key of Knowledge's size. Until the end of next turn, melee weapon attacks performed with the Key deal additional damage equal to the {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a target, to a maximum amount of damage equal to your proficiency bonus. It also gains the Reach weapon property, with that range being expanded by a further 5-ft. upon reaching 8th level in this class.

Quick attacks can be done with a quick palm, but you'd rather not dirty your hands when you can simply unlock a new way to attack. You may use your Bonus Action to perform an additional melee weapon attack with your Key by spending 1 Ki Point. Additionally, while you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you may use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier for skill checks pertaining to the latter attribute, including the Condition's bonus. You may also spend one {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to gain the same bonus to your {@skill Perception} checks for the next minute.

entries: If lost or destroyed, your Key of Knowledge can be re-made from a regular key over the course of a short or long rest.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: You may consider the Key of Knowledge as a magic item that can be given to an Artificer, Blacksmith or any other fitting craftsperson to work on and transform into a +1 monk weapon and so on for the sake of scaling until 11th level. Of course, gold cost may change harshly depending on campaign but we recommend having a base price 500 GP in materials for this +1 upgrade.

subclassFeature.name: To Grasp Erudition With One's Own Hands (Fist)
entries: {@i "Hold your gaze closer. We are not like the Keys; we are those who claim our knowledge through contact with our fists."}

You are of a sect which prefers to shield the hand the least amount possible toward anything it can touch, becoming an expert in the written word as well as the ways of a pugilist. You gain the following benefits when you choose this feature:

items: You may be bearing no armor or weapon, yet you quickly prove that others shouldn't judge you by your surprisingly tough cover. Your Unarmored Defense Armor Class increases by half your proficiency bonus.

It isn't just the prowess gained from burning knowledge that drives you on, its also the raw emotion of having to sacrifice such important things in the first place. You deal one {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you hit a creature with an unarmed attack as part of your Attack Action. This increases by one upon reaching 8th level in this class.

You aren't just a brawler boasting intelligence, you are also a keeper and protector of the relics of the mind. You may spend your Bonus Action while having at least 2 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count to grant yourself an amount of {@dice d6} Temporary Hit Points equal to your proficiency bonus by spending 2 Ki.

Defensive manoeuvres while being on the offense are still important, you have memorized that most efficiently. Whenever you perform a Flurry of Blows while having at least than 3 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count you gain {@dice 1d6} Temporary Hit Points that last for up to one minute outside of combat. This increases to {@dice 2d6} upon reaching 8th level in Monk and to {@dice 3d6} upon reaching 12th level in this class. This value sums with other Temporary Hit Points you may already have.

entries: Additionally, while you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you may use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength modifier for skill checks pertaining to the latter attribute, including the Condition's bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Reliquary of the Mind
entries: {@i "Mm. Indeed, I noticed on my stroll here that the sun had sunk beyond the horizon. Yet, it is said that erudition comes more naturally under the pale moonlight. I suppose I shall read now, then."}

The repertoire you have amassed over time regarding all manner of things has truly led you to become able to perform certain things that those that lack your knowledge would consider simply miraculous. You may spend your Ki points in the following ways:

items: You may spend 1 Ki point to cast the {@spell Detect Magic} spell. When you do so, instead of seeing auras around areas you instead manage to filter out every little detail that might be off about environment's natural order, such as realizing when wood has a mismatched texture of once being transmuted from stone or the lingering burn marks of a {@spell fireball} that was once evoked.

You may spend 3 Ki points to cast the {@spell Identify} spell without requiring its material cost. When you do so you also learn if the target has been cursed, yet you must pass an {@skill Arcana} check to determine its nature. ( As per the DM's discretion. ) Additionally you may recall what material was used for this items creation and its general region of origin, such as city or continent.

You may spend 6 Ki points to cast the {@spell Legend Lore} spell without requiring its material cost, instead only requiring a handful of books for research. You spend these Ki points after the casting time has been concluded.

entries: Instead of spending Ki points you may instead choose to spend {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, which each spent count accounting for 3 Ki.

Additionally you gain Proficiency in one Intelligence skill of your choice. You may choose a skill you have gained Proficiency in because of this feature as a choice for your Gathering Knowledge as Kindling feat, granting you Expertise with the skill until the next long rest instead.

subclassFeature.name: Body Fixation Studies (Fist)
entries: {@i "The hand is mightier than the key. I am certain that I have smote that understanding into them. And… Hm. I do not recall what I had planned to say hereafter."}

The fists that you use to tightly grip your knowhow have become something else, a tool to protect it - To impede anything else from smoothing your brain more than you already do. As long as you are unarmed and have Temporary Hit Points you gain Resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage.

Additionally, whenever you first gain Temporary Hit Points while having none you may choose to become Resistant to one of the following damage types for the same duration: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic or radiant.

subclassFeature.name: Unveil Information (Key)
entries: {@i "Good thinking. Let my key be the guide to your enlightenment."}

The way your Key processes light is unlike anything else you have seen, yet you have seen much through it and have learnt how to unveil the most through its vision. While wielding your Key you are considered to have Expertise in the {@skill Perception} skill and as a Free Action you may take once per turn or continuously out of combat you may use your Key as a looking glass, granting you Truesight toward a 30-ft. long cone in front of you. If you perceive any {@condition Invisible} or otherwise normally unseen creatures through this, you remember their location and they count as if they were not {@condition Invisible} to you until they move from that cone's reach.

subclassFeature.name: Mind of the Sacristan
entries: {@i "Records say that the Holy Relic, which we must protect with our lives, was discovered in the abyssal depths of the Ruins."}

Through rigorous training, learning and unlearning your mind has become a sacred temple to recycling knowledge - and as any polished reliquary it must find its relic to hold, as all the Saints of your Way have once come to do before you, to the purpose of acquiring all the knowledge that relic holds and to pave the way to those to come after you. You gain the following:

items: The determination to grasp more knowledge has become ingrained not only in your brain but your heart, granting you an additional count of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} whenever you gain it.

Your constant forgetting of all the things of which you must know to answer your calling have led you to develop an instinctual knowledge toward performing them. While you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you may add an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Skill Checks you aren't proficient in.

entries: Additionally, upon reaching this level you may spend a long rest to denominate a magic item of Very Rare or greater rarity to become your very own Relic, an object that you will do your utmost to keep protected from the world and all that would want it. You instantly gain all knowledge about its creation as if per the effects of the {@spell Legend Lore} spell and know perfectly how it works, as per the effects of the {@spell Identify} Spell.

Furthermore your Relic is considered to be an Artifact in rarity and your Attunement to it cannot be broken unless you die. If it provides a bonus modifier to attack or damage rolls, AC or DCs, that modifier increases by one. If it consumes Charges you only consume half the Charge cost the Relic would consume, rounded down and to a limit of one. If it already only costs one Charge to be activated, you may use the item's effects without spending Charges once per short or long rest.

You can instantly transport this item to your empty hand as a Free Action during your turn and always instinctively know its exact location provided it is within a mile of you. If your Relic is a weapon, you may add all its benefits to your unarmed attack provided it being carried by your person.
If your Relic is a Key of Knowledge, its Truesight range increases to become a 60-ft. cone and it instantly becomes a +4 weapon when chosen as your Relic.

subclassFeature.name: Spada Palermitana
entries: {@i "It don't matter even if I'm just a pale imitation. Gettin' stronger ain't what I'm trainin' my Palermitan Style for, anyway."}

The Palermitan Sword style is an art that few have learnt, and fewer have mastered - Being famous for its ability to draw oponents on one-on-one fights and through a series of escalating strikes bring the fight to a swift, victorious end. Those who embody the Spada Palermitana are just that - Pupils coming to not only become masters in such a style, but also becoming objects of power in their own right.

They usually are devout and perfectionists in their practice, being fast learners and unusually dedicated at their best but also easily creating bad tendencies to overwork or even reach the depths of their own self-worth, seeing any miniscule failure as a shame without equal.

subclassFeature.name: Il Cacciatore
entries: {@i "I'll show you an infinitely close approximation of your angle an' speed."}

A hunters discipline comes into effect not just with creating the perfect situation but with live studies of their prey, taking in their movements, their mistakes and their weaknesses as the hunt rages on - and you've made yourself adept at doing just that. While there is no more than one hostile creature within 5-ft. of you and no friendly creatures within the same range, you gain a count of {@condition Escalating Duel|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} whenever you first hit a creature during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: La Spada di Palermo
entries: {@i "… But she took me in and put a roof over my head. Fed me. Taught me this… bloody incredible swordfighting style—the sort a lowly vagrant like me would never have had the chance to learn."}

The Palermitan Style of Swordplay is an art form that you've got etched deep in your bones, your muscles swerving in pendulum arcs as naturally as you draw out your opponent's breath. This is done through dual weapons, allowing you to make perfected use of Two-Weapon Fighting:

items: You may wield two weapons without the prerequisite of one of them being Light, instead only requiring that neither weapon is Heavy.

Whenever you make an {@action Attack} as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules you still add half your ability modifier to the damage dealt. Whenever you do so, you inflict one count of {@condition Severed Tendons|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Severed Tendon} on your target.
When you Attune to a pair of magical weapons, they both count as a singular Attunement, taking only one slot and becoming Unattuned if either Attunement is broken.

entries: Additionally you may use once per turn the Force Into an Adequate Question attack in place of one of your Attacks as part of the Attack Action or Bonus Action. You may do so an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

entries.name: Force Into an Adequate Question
entries: You perform a swirling flurry of blows that aim not to hit the target, but instead funnel them toward a better positioning for you to benefit from. You perform an attack roll against the target, dealing damage as usual on a hit and having them instantly move up to 15-ft. in a line of your choice, or only 5-ft. on a missed attack roll. You instantly move to follow them. You both must move into unoccupied spaces and will not directly move into a space that would directly harm them, such as blazing ground or off a cliff.

subclassFeature.name: Manuale in Maturazione
entries: {@i "*exhale* What'd I tell you? Other styles ain't keepin' up with how fast the Palermitan style accelerates in a duel."}

As a fight rages on your body becomes a better and better blade to cut down your quarry, tempered in bloodshed and moved by sheer willpower. You gain additional effects per each passing round in combat:

items: {@b 2nd Round.} You gain an additional 5-ft. of movement speed.

{@b 3rd Round.} Your Armor Class increases by a bonus modifier of 1 and you may now spend your Bonus Action to perform two melee weapon attacks instead, but you inflict one less count of any Condition you would inflict and do not add your ability modifier to their damage rolls. ( If you would deal greater than 2 counts of any Condition, you deal only half instead. )
{@b 4th Round.} You gain an additional 5-ft. of movement speed.
{@b 5th Round.} Your attacks deal an additional Condition count whenever you would inflict them through melee weapon attacks.

entries: These effects are cumulative and end alongside a combat. Additionally, your knowledge-gathering ability has extended beyond simply going through the motions in a short-term manner, instead also focusing on amassing the needed knowledge to support your general repertoire. You gain proficiency in one Skill of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Cacciatore del Traguardo
entries: {@i "Witness a demonstration of the Palermitan dismantling technique."}
{@i "Sezionatura di Cervo!"}

The Palermitan style is flashy, often being considered one without restraint or even an oblique facsimile of swordsmanship as an art form to ill-tongues. You've grown to show them wrong, perfecting a series of movements and blocks to make them swallow such words of disrespect toward your tradition. You may perform a Finisher Move that replace the last attack you could make in your turn, requiring you to have hit the same target twice before attempting to your choice of one of the following Finishers:

items: {@b Broken Spear.} Much like a butcher will find a means to use bone and marrow alike, you treat your weapons as tool shards to drive in the sides of your target. You instantly make two melee weapon attacks against a target within reach, then dealing an additional damage die and inflicting one more Condition count on a hit.

{@b Death Mask.} You prepare a series of feints and deceptive strikes to hide your aim for the true goal, a decisive lobotomy through a pierced head. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach at the start of your next turn, reducing your Critical Threshold for each time you were targeted by a hostile creature's attack or spell until then. ( You deal a Critical Hit on a roll of 19-20 if targeted once, 18-20 if twice and so on. )

{@b House as a Fortress.} You ready your blades, not for the sake of attacking the target themselves but instead debilitating their every blow so they may truly feel helpless. You gain a bonus modifier to your Armor Class equal to your proficiency bonus until the start of your next turn.

{@b Sea Urchine.} You deliver deft strikes to the opponents feet, binding them to this duel and of course, their early demise. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach. On a hit their movement speed and Dexterity Saving Throw modifier are halved until the end of your next turn.

entries: You may use your Bonus Action Attack for this finishing blow, and may make use of them for an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest. Whenever you kill a creature using one such Finisher move you regain its use.

You may instantly trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target of your Finisher when you deal damage to them, or instead choose to convert all their {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. count into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead.

subclassFeature.name: Senzionatura di Inefficienza
entries: {@i "As the propriety of honorable combat dictates… One daft prick at a time."}

Slicing at enemies isn't enough. Your blade has turned inward to chop off any little mistakes you would once commit in your swordplay, disregarding any weight that may come to be unbearable on you. You gain the following:

items: You make sure your opening strikes are as dazzling and damaging as your finishing blows. Whenever you deal damage to a creature, they suffer 2 {@condition Severed Tendons|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Severed Tendon} count if they were not suffering from the Condition.

Although a cadence must still be built, you always draw your first move with the upper hand in mind. You add your proficiency bonus to your Initiative modifier and you may perform replace any one of your attacks with a Finishing Move during your first turn, despite how many times you have hit a target.

Constant exhaustion from your relentless training in the style has led you to be more resistant than most, granting you the ability to reduce your current Exhaustion Points by one at the end of combat, for a maximum of twice per short or long rest.

There is an undeniable rush to being in constant combat, moving from duel to duel in the battlefield - Whenever you kill a creature, you may use your Reaction to instantly recover {@dice 1d8} plus your proficiency bonus' worth of Hit Points.into unoccupied spaces and will not directly move into a space that would directly harm them, such as blazing ground or off a cliff.

subclassFeature.name: Vengeance Martial Archetype
entries: {@i “Heh. Why work with your brains when you've got the brawn?”}

The Vengeance Martial Archetype is selfish and unstoppable. You want personal vengeance against the world, and other people around you are just pawns for you to sacrifice in order to achieve that vengeance and the heights of greatness.

You belong to the Middle, a faction that treats all of their members like family, and mistreating one of theirs earns the ire of the entire group. Within, family forgives tiny missteps, but outsiders do not receive such mercy. However, you also believe thay a little sacrifice is nothing for the family, and will use your brothers and sisters to aid in your ascension, even if that costs them their lives.

Vengeance Fighters are very strong, but also uncaring. They trick you into believing you're a part of their inner circle, then use you for their own gains. You may play as a character that eventually comes to realize the wrong in their ways, but remember to always keep a desire for vengeance deep within your heart.

subclassFeature.name: The Book of Vengeance
entries: {@i “Kiddo, remember what Mama told you? You ever find anything you don't like, you can talk to me about it!”}

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the end of the first round of combat.

Whenever you hit an enemy with counts of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Sealed Sword [Lævateinn]
entries: {@i “Hah. What's a couple of pointed fingers when this sword of legends… is resting all snug and sweet in my hands?”}

You have discovered a legendary relic, but its power is currently sealed. The mythical Greatsword {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} requires a specific type of user to attune with it. You are no such user, but you will still attempt to draw out as much power from it as you can. You have the {@item Sealed Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Greatsword, you are always attuned to it and it cannot be destroyed. If it is lost, you can magically teleport it to your location during a Long Rest.
When you attack a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with your {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may choose one of the following options once per turn:

items: They suffer 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per turn the first time you or another Middle member would inflict them with {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the start of your next turn;

They suffer 1 additional count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} per turn the first time you or another Middle member would inflict them with {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} until the start of your next turn;
If there is a Rogue that follows the Middle's Blade Roguish Archetype that you can see within 30 feet of you, you may give them 1 count of Thermal Blades;

If there is a Rogue that follows the Middle's Blade Roguish Archetype that you can see within 30 feet of you, you may show off to them, adding {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage to your attacks until the end of your turn.

entries: You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Stomping
entries: {@i “Welcome to the kill zone!”}

As a member of the Middle, you do not lack the powerful magical tattoos they are known to boast. You may attune to an additional number of tattoos equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. Additionally, whenever you finish a Short or a Long Rest, you may choose 3 tattoos from the list below to have active (if any of them requires a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Tattoo of Manipulation
entries: Upon getting this Tattoo, you gain proficiency in the Persuasion or the Deception skill, your choice. If you already have Proficiency in the chosen skill, you gain Expertise instead.

entries.name: Tattoo of Deep Wounds
entries: When you hit a creature, you may choose to inflict the {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} condition on them as long as they have {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts. Once they are cured of the {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} condition, they become Immune to it for 10 minutes. {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead causes the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the previous Condition and 2 stacks are removed every time it is triggered. The Medicine Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

entries.name: Tattoo of Dread
entries: As a Bonus Action, each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you and aware of you must succeed on Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, they become Immune to this effect for the next 24 hours. Creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} have disadvantage on this saving throw.

entries.name: Tattoo of Stomping
entries: You may replace one of your attack actions with an unarmed attack, which you are proficient with, against a creature within reach. On a hit, they take {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and are pushed 10 feet back towards a direction of your choice. This forced movement provokes opportunity attacks, and the damage increases to {@damage 1d10} at level 10 and {@damage 1d12} at level 15.

entries.name: Tattoo of Alliance
entries: For each Middle-aligned friendly creature within 30 feet of you, you gain a +1 bonus to your ability checks, for a maximum of +3.

entries.name: Tattoo of Shielding
entries: You gain +1 to your AC.

entries.name: Tattoo of Chains
entries: As a Reaction when you see a creature move within 30 feet of you, you may attempt to Grapple them from where you are with your chains of loyalty. Creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} have disadvantage on this ability check.

entries.name: Tattoo of Rule Violation
entries: At the start of combat, before any turns take place, you may establish a rule. If that rule is broken by a creature, you can use your Reaction to glare at them, lowering your sunglasses if you are wearing any. They must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition Paralyzed} until the end of your next turn due to your overwhelming presence. Creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} have disadvantage on this saving throw. After a creature is affected by this Paralysis, they become Immune to it for 24 hours.

entries.name: Tattoo of Resentment
entries: You have advantage on your first attack every turn against creatures with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

entries.name: Designer's Notes
entries: Your rules for the Tattoo of Rule Violation can be anything you find fitting, but your DM has the final say if something is or isn't allowed. Breathing would not be a fun rule violation most of the time, but it COULD be interesting if used once for a cool roleplaying situation. Basically, make cool rules that everyone at the table can agree with, don't take the fun out of the ability!

subclassFeature.name: Don't Let Something Like This Break You!
entries: {@i “I don't need some stupid crutch like that “Core Burst (心)” crap. I just gotta pull as much power as I can from these tattoos and grit my teeth, and I'll overpower your fancy little tricks no problem.”}

You live in a dangerous world, so your solution was to become the most dangerous thing within it and not just survive, but rule it. Whenever you use your {@classFeature Second Wind|Fighter|PHB|1} ability when you have half of your hit points or less, for 1 minute you gain Resistance to all damage types except Psychic or Force, and the first time you hit an attack every turn, you heal hit points equal to {@dice 1d10} + your constitution modifier.
When you use this ability, you can only use it again after a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Stamp of Vengeance
entries: {@i “Heh. Why work with your brains when you've got the brawn?”}

You don't take shit from anyone, or anything, and you make that very clear with every step you take. Your speed increases by 10 feet. After you use your {@classFeature Indomitable|Fighter|PHB|9} ability, regardless of if you failed or succeeded, you may immediately use your remaining movement speed to move towards the source that forced you to make a saving throw. You can make an unarmed attack against it, as if you had your Tattoo of Stomping active, except it deals double the damage dice. If the source is an object or a structure, it takes double damage from this attack.

Additionally, if you have taken the {@optfeature Fighting Style: Sacrifice|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may choose to double the damage dice of your attack once per Long Rest, but both creatures will take the doubled damage, and it cannot be diminished or prevented in any way by the friendly creature. If the friendly creature is a Middle's Blade Rogue, then both them and the creature become Vulnerable to the damage types of your attack as well.

subclassFeature.name: I'll Gut You Like a Fish
entries: {@i “Hahahahaha! Having a good time, Kiddo? Mama's the best, huh?”}

You've heard the destructive desire of the sword would eventually corrupt your spirit - bullshit, you're as sane as the day you killed for this thing. As long as you're holding {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you gain the following abilities:

entries.name: Gut Stab [Lævateinn]
entries: If you are Grappling a creature, you gain advantage on attack rolls against it. Additionally, if you hit 3 or more attacks against the Grappled creature, they must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they gain an Internal Injury from the Lingering Injuries table. On a successful save, they instead receive a Festering Wound.

entries.name: Complete and Total Extermination [Lævateinn]
entries: As an Action, you can make an attack roll against a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If it hits, you throw your sword at them, piercing their gut and dealing {@damage 3d8} Piercing damage and {@damage 3d8} Fire damage, as well as 8 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. They must then make a Constitution saving throw as you attempt to cleave the sword out of them. On a failed save, they take an additional {@damage 5d8} Slashing damage and you sever one of their limbs off in a non-lethal way. If this would reduce them to 0 hit points, you bissect them instead, melting their insides. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Screaming Melody
entries: {@i “I know it hurts, but please, stop struggling…!”}
{@i “I promise, nothing could make as fascinating music as a human can… Nothing!”}

Rockin' is all that a bard of the magnanimous and great COLLEGE OF THE SCREAMING MELODY needs to be alive, to be able to shred flesh with metal and have music be performed by each dying noise and beating gargle of another - Ah! Pure ecstasy.

Of course, people - MOST people don't understand the artistry at work upon taking apart the human body to find the music inside, so these bards either take to being secretive in their work, only forming the occasional band perofrmance with their fellows or they swing the complete other way in an obsessive opulence that rivals even that of paladins!

subclassFeature.name: Shredding Melodies
entries: {@i “I promise, nothing could make as fascinating music as a human can… Nothing!”}

Music isn't just an art form limited to the conveniently well-accepted instruments that all other bards partake in playing, no, hardly! You have come to understand that there is no greater song machine other than the meticulous inner-workings of living beings when they are subject to glorious torment, and you have done your utmost to become proficient in playing them!

You may perform melodic attacks as an Action during your turn provided you are wielding an Instrument you are proficient in. A melodic attack is an advanced artform comprised of absolutely shredding with your instruments, blowing your targets minds or even setting them ablaze with sheer, overwhelming fervour for the melody. You are proficient with these attacks and use your Charisma modifier for their rolls, dealing {@damage 2d4} plus your Charisma modifier's worth of thunder damage on a hit, also inflicting 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
You may choose which of the Conditions to inflict and how to partition them. The amount inflicted increases to 3 count upon reaching 8th level in Bard.
You start being able to perform a single melodic attack during your turn and upon reaching 6th level your melodious attacks count as magical for the purposes of bypassing Resistance,

Whenever a creature benefits from your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} you may instantly perform a melodic attack as a Reaction against a target within 30-ft. of them, provided they can hear you.

subclassFeature.name: Hype up the Masses!
entries: {@i “If everyone threw their bodies into me, it'll certainly create an even sweeter melody”}

A lively life is one that is marched with an entire band and not a single sad little player, after all, how are you going to play without plentiful instruments?! That thought has crawled in the back of your mind enough times for you to consider the occasional welcoming of others into your melody and actually learning how they tick from the outside in. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient. Charisma is your Ability Modifier for this skill.

Additionally, whenever a creature attempts a Strength, Dexterity, Constitution or Charisma ability check you may spent your Reaction to play a backing track to hype them - and yourself - up, granting them half your Charisma modifier as a bonus modifier to their roll. If they still fail, the sounds of their broken body fill you with joy, with that creature suffering an amount of {@damage d8} bludgeoning damage equal to half their proficiency bonus and you instantly recovering one use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1}. This must be done before they roll. You may only use this feature an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Rampant Melody
entries: {@i “This way, just a little closer… Hahah! Perfect! That scream, weaving into a ninth chord!”}
{@i “Such wondrous… harmony.”}

Ah, the sweet, sweet and tender dance of notes fluttering down your instrument is ecstasy for your brain! However, you have come to learn that the true bliss comes from creating a twinned harmony by pulling the cords of other's bodies, mangling them to make truly divine music! Whenever you make a melodious attack for the first time during your turn, you may perform an additional melodious attack as part of the same action for each time you've rolled a 20 or greater on the dice roll, including modifiers. This value is diminished by one per melodious attack hit as part of this Action, with it being reset at the end of your turn. You may make one additional attack at 6th level and a second upon reaching 12th level in Bard. You may select the same creature as the target of these additional attacks.

You have a +1 bonus modifier to this roll for each sum of 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count the target is suffering from, to a maximum value of +5. This is considered a direct increase to your roll's base result for the sakes of triggering additional attacks.
When you perform your first melodious attack during your turn you may spend a Bard spell slot to empower your music. You gain the following as part of this Action:

items: Your range increases by 5-ft. and you may choose an additional target per spell slot level spent.
You perform an additional melodious attack for every two spell slot levels spent greater than 0, such as performing two additional melodious attacks when spending a 4th level spell slot.

Instead of delivering more notes and performing additional melodious attacks whenever you've rolled the aforementioned value on a dice roll, you instead inflict 2 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count whenever you trigger that roll. This value increases by one for each time you have triggered this additional infliction.

If cast using a 4th level spell slot or higher, you also convert all {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target to be {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead. Additionally, you add your Charisma modifier to damage rolls of melodious attacks.

If cast using an 8th level spell slot or higher, you perform an additional melodious attack for each creature killed as part of this Action. Summoned or otherwise easily-reproducible creatures do not count toward this, as a fake being just does not provide anything but repetitive music to your ears.

If cast using a 9th level spell slot, you deal additional damage on hits equal to your choice of the targets {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Additionally, you recover a spent {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} for each creature killed through this attack, to a maximum amount recovered equal to half your maximum Bardic Inspiration die. Summoned creatures also do not count toward this.

entries: Additionally, you have learnt how to create such electrifying symphonies that they touch the hearts of legions at once. Whenever you grant a creature a use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} dice, you may choose to fill another creature within 30-ft. of that target with inspiration. When you do so, though, your attempt at catering to multiple tastes slightly diminishes the quality of the music, granting each only a {@dice d4}. This increases to a {@dice d6} upon reaching 15th level in Bard.

subclassFeature.name: Rhythmaniac
entries: {@i “Make me move… Light my path with the songs!”}

No one should, could or would stop you now, they can't stop either when the rhythm that pervades their soul! Your jam sessions have evolved, short strums to melodies to whole shows played over the battle stage and others finally have a shot of truly, lastingly connecting to the song that rips at your heart's strings! At the end of your turns, all creatures who have spent a use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} die during this combat may choose to gain one count of {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. While creatures have this Condition you are considered to be Concentrating on it, with all creatures' count being lost if you lose Concentration. This counts an additional Concentration for the purpose of still being able to concentrate on other spells.

A creature with this Condition has been enraptured by the god-rending melody of your carnage, and can't help but want to partake in it as musician and instrument, dealing and suffering an additional amount of damage equal to your Charisma modifier whenever they deal or suffer damage ( respectively ) equal to your 3 times your {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count that they currently have. Whenever a creature declines receiving {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they halve the counts of the Condition they currently have, rounded up. Additionally, if a creature with this Condition benefits from your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} rolls the minimum value rolled is always equal to their current {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, being increased if it was lower.

A creature with {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} gain an additional count whenever they first kill a creature during a round, except for summoned creatures. Additionally, a creature with 3 or more count may spend one count to perform an additional weapon attack or cast an additional spell of 3rd level or lower during their turn.

While out of combat you may grant a creature up to 4 {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count whenever they receive one of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1}s. When used like this, they gain a +1 to skill checks for each count they currently have, although they can't help but feel the loathsome break in their cadence whenever they fail those, suffering {@damage 1d6} psychic damage for each count they currently have and then instantly losing the Condition.

Additionally, you may spend your Action while within 5-ft. of a medium or greater corpse to perform a haunting melody using it. When you do so, you instantly lose any negative Conditions currently afflicting you and gain 3 {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. Any hostile creatures within 30-ft. of you that can see or hear you must also pass a Wisdom saving throw or suffer {@damage 4d8} psychic damage from the horrible sight. While you have {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count you recover an amount of Hit Points equal to the Condition's count at the end of your turns. If you lose Concentration you suffer an amount of {@damage d6} psychic damage equal to all {@condition Rhythm|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count lost.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Loyalty
entries: {@i “Damn, passed out already, huh. Now that grudge is going into the Book of Vengeance... I'll avenge you soon.”}

Paladins that follow the Oath of Loyalty have a duty to their companions, their family. They will raise them to become the best versions of themselves and protect them from all harm. In return, their bonds will become unbreakable, and there will be no battle great enough to bring them down.

The faction of the Middle, an organization that preaches that all who are a part of it are siblings and must be there for each other, while avenging every misdeed done to its members, is where these Paladins usually hail from. This organization can be flavored however you want in your world, if it even exists, but it must maintain the familial ties that its members follow.

While a Paladin that follows the Oath of Loyalty will never forgive a mistake committed against them by those who are not family, it is generally considered right to look the other way and forgive your siblings for their errors. After all, family is family, and blood is thicker than water.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Loyalty
entries: {@i “The Middle remembers. It doesn't matter what I did here; the Middle will remember everyone and everything that dared to turn their back on it.”}
The tenets of a Paladin that assumes the Oath of Loyalty require an unshakable bond between them and their family.
{@b Never Forget.} If slights were committed against your family, write them down in the book of vengeance. Never allow whoever dared to stand against one of your siblings to see the light of day.

{@b Love Your Siblings.} Your brothers and sisters are your loyal family and must be treated with respect. Their slights can be forgiven, and they deserve compliments and rewards when successfully achieving their goals and your own.

{@b Recover What Was Stolen!} This is an optional Tenet. You might have lost something extremely precious to you, like hair coupons to an incredible salon of complete and total lusciousness. You and your family will hunt this thief to the ends of the earth, and you will make sure they pays for their crimes.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Iron Maiden
entries: Druidism is regarded as an ancient tradition relating to the natural world and sometimes even abhoring that of technological advancement that stiffles that natural growth of all things. Despite that, or even because of that there is a small, peculiar circle of druids which choose to embrace that technology - that so called tainted metal to replicate nature itself, a controversial medium for a pure passion of this so called “artwork”.

Those which follow the circle of the Iron Maiden have stripped themselves of their supple flesh and instead addorn it as material for their creations, embellishing the natural world with their very self for the sake of spreading their unbridled joy and vision of the world around them. They also do such in a way that encapsulates the moment of lightning striking the ground or a volcano erupting - a slow, deliberate sudden moment where they may spend months and years under their iron shell only to enrichen a glimpse of the presence of their body underneath.
They may not be well seen in druid communities, but one thing is certain: the passion these folk have for their art is unrivaled, going toe to toe with even that of a bards love for the arts.

subclassFeature.name: Biomimeticism: Art Imitates Life
entries: {@i “Aesthetics concerns itself entirely with the visible, yet this self-evident familiarity often invites neglect that overlooks the inherent significance of what is seen...”}

You are a very unique type of druid, the one who wishes to transcend the binds of their flesh by imitating nature the best they can: constructing and shaping a body sculpted in the image of what once was. You, unlike the vast majority of other circles, embrace the touch of metal while extracting and re-shaping the natural form to become a better meld of your view of reality.

As a form of repression to better understand the limits of your body, you've stowed away the fruits of your slow labour into a metallic armor that paradoxically hides and defines your form. You are always in this Iron Maiden Form until you spend one of your Wildshape uses as a Bonus Action to enter your Flowing State Form, as per described in the Features below.

You, however, do not limit yourself to using your own body as material, also acquiring one {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} after such. You may spend count for the following:

items: You may spend up to your proficiency bonus' amount of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} before performing an attack to deal an additional 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on a hit per {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spent.

You may spend up to half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} before performing an attack to gain a bonus modifier to hit equal to half your proficiency bonus.

entries: Additionally, your obsession with the humanoid form doesn't stop only at your art, no, your imitation of life extends to what you see from other beings. Whenever you use the Wildshape feature you may transform into Humanoids instead of Beasts, following the usual rules for the Feature. If the Humanoid would be carrying any items in its monster sheet, you create exact copies of them as long as they aren't unique to that creature, and if you copy something akin to a wizard's grimoire, you have the practical content of their spells in Druidic, but not any personal notes and such. Your appearance is always metallic and can be discerned easily to be an imitation by other creatures.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This subclass is intended to be played while locking you out of the usual Wildshape rules to turn into Beasts. If for any reason you'd rather maintain this for your druid, consider that you alter your Form as if the metallic plates that compose your body shifted and melded together to become whatever animal you wish to become, instead of being the usual magical transformation.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of Loyalty Spells table. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work.
